dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: My grandmother wrote a novel when she was young. She never showed it to anyone.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Really? What is it about?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: It's about a cat who saves a village. She says it really happened when she was a child.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A cat saving a village? That sounds like a miracle.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: I have lived here all my life, and I never heard this story until last Saturday, when she finally told me.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Where did she keep it?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: On a shelf in the kitchen, behind some old clothes and curtains.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, but I don't believe it. Cats don't save villages.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: She believed the story, though. My grandfather told it to her every summer.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Maybe he just wanted to feel special. Such things happen every day; people change stories.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Maybe. But she signed the last page with 'This is true.'

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That's strange. Did anything else happen in the story?

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Yes! The cat bit a snake before it could reach the children playing near the beach.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: A snake? Now I really don't believe it.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Wait, look outside! There's a cat sitting by the door, and it looks just like the one in the novel.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: That can't be the same cat. It's just a normal cat.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it just bit a snake right by the door, the same as in the story.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Okay, okay. I believe you now. This is a good story, and I feel warm just hearing it.

dialogue.speaker: Alex
dialogue.text: See? Some things you just have to believe, even without proof.

dialogue.speaker: Sam
dialogue.text: Well, tomorrow I will read the whole novel myself, from morning until midday if I have to!
